William Shakespeare, Hamlet.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/william-shakespeare/hamlet

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- William Shakespeare, the author, died 1616 (United Kingdom (first published London, 1603/1604 quartos; colophon dates the edition used to 1600)).

First publication of the text used: 1600 (colophon: 'published in 1600 by William Shakespeare').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1600, before 1931;
  a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after
  publication, so this work entered it in 1695.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom (first published London, 1603/1604 quartos; colophon dates the edition used to 1600)): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years
  after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die
  did so in 1616, so the work entered the public domain there on
  1 January 1687.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- colophon states 1600
- Wikidata Q692 William Shakespeare died 1616
- colophon mentions 'Emendations to the text are provided by Open Source Shakespeare' - a textual source, not new wording by a named modern person; no translator or introducer named
